title: Which AI startups actually land enterprise contracts? — Brian Lewis, Millennium
talk_summary: A hedge-fund product lead describes what makes AI vendors fail enterprise procurement: efficacy, security, reliability, and legal gates, with only ~5% of demo calls converting to contracts.

takeaways.technique: Per-agent entitlements and scoped permissions instead of blanket access
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat agent entitlements as a first-class problem: agents must inherit scoped, auditable permissions rather than read/write-all defaults, because rogue agents multiply existing entitlement failures.
takeaways.evidence_quote: agents inherit your foundations... agents are going to like 100X that problem

takeaways.technique: Thin agents over a smarter shared substrate
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue for centralized, easily consumable knowledge (docs, support articles, company context) so agents stay thin and the substrate carries shared state, rather than each agent re-embedding context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need thinner agents and a smarter substrate... centralized knowledge is really key to that

takeaways.technique: Audit logs and controlled rollout for config changes
takeaways.what_they_do: They require every admin setting to be API-accessible, audit-logged on change, and rollable-back, because rapid multi-times-a-day shipping without version tracking makes failures untraceable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we want to see audit logs on config changes... we want to be able to control the rollout on these changes

takeaways.what_they_do: Pilot timelines collapsed from 6 months to ~2 weeks, and the buyer, not the vendor, defines success criteria up front.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we define the success criteria, not the vendor

takeaways.technique: Explicit failure-mode checklist as acceptance gate
takeaways.what_they_do: He enumerates concrete failure modes vendors exhibit (vaporware, no ETAs, beta-only features with permissive retention, no status page) as a checklist buyers apply.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the worst AI startups don't have any security architecture diagrams, no path to a support engineer, no deployment control or audit logs, no ETAs

takeaways.what_they_do: When legacy-to-target gap is large, they stand up a separate environment to test what works before committing, rather than experimenting in production.
takeaways.evidence_quote: maybe we need a separate ecosystem to do a lot of this work, figure out what does work and what doesn't
